# Typeform vs Formbricks (2026)

## Overview
Typeform and Formbricks are both online form and survey tools that help businesses and individuals collect data and feedback from their audience. This comparison is beneficial for those looking to switch from a proprietary solution to a self-hosted, open-source alternative, with the core use case being data collection and analysis. The key reason someone would switch is to gain full control over their data and reduce costs.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Typeform offers a free plan with limited features, while Formbricks is completely free and open-source, with the option to self-host.
* Data ownership: Formbricks allows users to have full control over their data, while Typeform stores data on its servers.
* Setup complexity: Typeform has a more user-friendly interface and is easier to set up, while Formbricks requires more technical expertise to self-host.
* Scalability: Formbricks can be scaled vertically by increasing server resources, while Typeform has built-in scalability features.
* Integration difference: Typeform has native integrations with popular marketing tools, while Formbricks supports integrations through APIs and webhooks.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Typeform | Formbricks |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | Free / $25-$83/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | AGPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | Approximately $1.25-$4.15 per user (billed annually) | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | Approximately $1.25-$4.15 per user (billed annually) | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
### Typeform
* Easy to use and set up
* Native integrations with popular marketing tools
* Scalable and reliable infrastructure
* Limited control over data storage and security
* Costs can add up for large teams or high-volume usage
### Formbricks
* Fully open-source and self-hosted
* Complete control over data storage and security
* Highly customizable and extensible
* Requires technical expertise to set up and maintain
* Limited native integrations with marketing tools

## When to Choose Each
Typeform is a good choice for small to medium-sized teams that need a user-friendly and scalable form and survey tool, with native integrations with popular marketing tools. It's ideal for teams that prioritize ease of use and don't mind paying for a proprietary solution. On the other hand, Formbricks is suitable for larger teams or organizations that require full control over their data and are willing to invest time and resources into setting up and maintaining a self-hosted solution.

## Migration Path
1. Export your Typeform data in CSV or JSON format.
2. Set up a Formbricks instance on your server or use a cloud provider.
3. Use the Formbricks import tool to migrate your data from the exported file.
4. Configure any necessary integrations or customizations in Formbricks.
5. Test your forms and surveys to ensure everything is working as expected.

## Our Take
Formbricks is not yet production-ready for most users, as it requires technical expertise to set up and maintain. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that Formbricks lacks native support for certain question types, such as matrix questions. However, for teams that value data ownership and customization, Formbricks is a viable alternative to Typeform, and we recommend switching if you have the technical resources to support it.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams that don't need native integrations with marketing tools
* Medium-sized teams that prioritize data ownership and security
* Large teams that require high customization and extensibility
* Organizations with in-house technical expertise
* Businesses that need to reduce costs and avoid vendor lock-in

## FAQ
### Can I use Formbricks for free?
Yes, Formbricks is completely free and open-source, with the option to self-host.
### Is Formbricks as easy to use as Typeform?
No, Formbricks requires more technical expertise to set up and maintain.
### Can I integrate Formbricks with popular marketing tools?
Yes, Formbricks supports integrations through APIs and webhooks, but may require more development effort.
### Is my data secure with Formbricks?
Yes, Formbricks allows you to have full control over your data storage and security.
### Can I migrate my Typeform data to Formbricks?
Yes, you can export your Typeform data in CSV or JSON format and import it into Formbricks using the import tool.

# Miro vs Excalidraw (2026)

## Overview
Miro and Excalidraw are two popular tools used for collaborative whiteboarding and diagramming, benefiting teams and individuals who need to visualize and work on projects together. The core use case for both tools is to facilitate real-time collaboration and idea generation. Someone would switch from Miro to Excalidraw to gain more control over their data and hosting.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Miro offers a free plan and paid plans starting at $8-$16 per user per month, while Excalidraw is completely free.
* Data ownership: Excalidraw allows users to self-host and have complete control over their data, whereas Miro stores data on its proprietary servers.
* Setup complexity: Miro has a more user-friendly and straightforward setup process, while Excalidraw requires more technical expertise to self-host.
* Scalability: Miro is designed to handle large teams and enterprises, while Excalidraw is better suited for smaller teams and individuals.
* Integration difference: Miro has a wider range of integrations with popular tools and services, while Excalidraw has a more limited set of integrations.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Miro | Excalidraw |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | Free / $8-$16/user/month | Free |
| License | Proprietary | MIT |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $400-$800/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $1,600-$3,200/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
### Miro
* Pros:
	+ User-friendly interface
	+ Wide range of integrations
	+ Scalable for large teams
	+ Collaborative features
	+ Mobile app
* Cons:
	+ Limited control over data
	+ Expensive for large teams
	+ Limited customization options
	+ Proprietary license
### Excalidraw
* Pros:
	+ Completely free
	+ Self-hosting option
	+ Open-source license
	+ High degree of customization
	+ Control over data
* Cons:
	+ Limited integrations
	+ Steeper learning curve
	+ Limited support resources
	+ Not suitable for large teams
	+ Limited mobile support

## When to Choose Each
Miro is a good choice for large teams and enterprises that need a scalable and user-friendly collaboration platform with a wide range of integrations. It is also suitable for teams that prioritize ease of use and are willing to pay for the convenience. Excalidraw, on the other hand, is a good choice for smaller teams and individuals who value control over their data and are comfortable with self-hosting and customization. It is also suitable for teams on a tight budget who need a free collaboration platform.

## Migration Path
1. Export your Miro boards as SVG or CSV files.
2. Set up an Excalidraw server or use a hosted instance.
3. Import your SVG or CSV files into Excalidraw using the built-in import tool.
4. Configure any necessary settings and customize your Excalidraw instance.
5. Invite your team to join and start collaborating on Excalidraw.

## Our Take
Excalidraw is not yet production-ready for most users due to its limited support resources and lack of polish in some areas. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that Excalidraw's self-hosting option requires a significant amount of technical expertise, which may be a barrier for some users. However, for teams and individuals who value control over their data and are comfortable with self-hosting and customization, Excalidraw is a viable alternative to Miro, and we recommend switching to take advantage of its free and open-source nature.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams (less than 10 users) who need a free collaboration platform and do not require a wide range of integrations.
* Individuals who value control over their data and are comfortable with self-hosting.
* Teams on a tight budget who need a collaboration platform with minimal costs.
* Developers who prefer open-source software and are comfortable with customization.
* Teams who do not need mobile support and are primarily working on desktop devices.

## FAQ
### Can I use Excalidraw for large teams?
No, Excalidraw is not suitable for large teams due to its limited scalability and lack of support resources.
### Is Excalidraw completely free?
Yes, Excalidraw is completely free, with no costs or fees for using the software.
### Can I self-host Excalidraw?
Yes, Excalidraw offers a self-hosting option, which allows users to have complete control over their data and hosting.
### Does Excalidraw have mobile support?
Limited mobile support is available for Excalidraw, but it is not as polished as the desktop version.
### Can I import my Miro boards into Excalidraw?

title: Netlify vs Coolify
comparison_markdown:
# Netlify vs Coolify

## Overview

Popular platform for deploying and hosting web apps and static sites. is a popular proprietary tool in the developer-tools space. Coolify is a free, open-source alternative that gives organizations complete control over their data and deployment.

## Key Differences

- **Cost**: Netlify costs Free / $19-$99/month; Coolify is Free (self-hosted)
- **License**: Netlify is Proprietary; Coolify is Apache 2.0
- **Data ownership**: Coolify can be self-hosted so your data stays on infrastructure you control
- **Vendor lock-in**: Coolify eliminates dependency on a single commercial vendor
- **Community**: Coolify has an active open-source community contributing features and fixes

## Pricing Comparison

| Aspect | Netlify | Coolify |
|--------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Base pricing | Free / $19-$99/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | Apache 2.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Cost at 50 users | See pricing page | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Cost at 200 users | See pricing page | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Vendor lock-in | High | None |

## Pros and Cons

### Netlify

**Pros:**
- Polished, professionally designed user interface
- Large ecosystem of official integrations
- Managed infrastructure with no server maintenance required
- Enterprise SLA and dedicated support available
- Mobile apps are well-maintained and reliable

**Cons:**
- Significant per-user monthly cost that scales linearly with team size
- Your data is stored on the vendor infrastructure
- No ability to inspect or modify the source code
- Feature roadmap controlled entirely by the vendor
- Risk of pricing changes, acquisition, or discontinuation

### Coolify

**Pros:**
- Free to self-host with costs only for server infrastructure
- Complete data ownership and privacy control
- Source code is auditable and modifiable
- Active open-source community
- No vendor lock-in or risk of sudden pricing changes
> GitHub: [coollabsio/coolify](https://github.com/coollabsio/coolify) * ~35k stars

**Cons:**
- Requires technical knowledge to self-host and maintain
- May lack some advanced features found in the proprietary version
- Support relies on community forums rather than a paid helpdesk
- UI polish may lag behind the proprietary tool
- You are responsible for updates, backups, and security patches

## When to Choose Each

**Choose Netlify if:** Netlify is the right choice when you need the most polished user experience, the broadest integration ecosystem, and professional support with SLA guarantees.

**Choose Coolify if:** Coolify is ideal for privacy-conscious teams, organizations with strict data sovereignty requirements, or anyone wanting to eliminate per-seat subscription costs.

## Migration Path

Export your data from Netlify in its standard export format, review Coolify import documentation, and plan a pilot period where both tools run in parallel.

## Our Take

Coolify is production-ready for most teams willing to invest a few hours in setup. The self-hosted version gives you identical or better functionality to the paid Netlify tiers, with no recurring per-seat cost.

The main technical limitation worth knowing: you are responsible for your own backups, updates, and uptime. If your server goes down, so does your Coolify instance. Plan for this with automated backups and a monitoring alert.

Our recommendation: if your team has at least one developer and you are paying more than $100/month for Netlify, switching to self-hosted Coolify will pay for itself within the first month. If nobody on your team is comfortable with Linux or Docker, stay on Netlify until you have that resource.

## Who Should Switch

- Startups under 20 people paying per-seat fees they cannot yet justify
- Dev teams who already self-host other tools and have the ops knowledge
- Organizations in jurisdictions with strict data residency requirements
- Teams who have evaluated Netlify paid features and only use the basics
- Founders and solopreneurs who want the functionality without the subscription

## FAQ

### Is Coolify free to use?
Yes. Coolify is free to self-host. Your only cost is the server, typically $6-$12/month on a VPS provider like DigitalOcean or Vultr.

### How hard is it to migrate from Netlify to Coolify?
For most teams, migration takes 2-4 hours. Export your Netlify data, follow the Coolify import guide, and test with a small group before switching everyone over.

### Does Coolify get regular updates?
Yes. Coolify has an active open-source community with regular releases. Check the GitHub repository for release frequency.

### Can I use Coolify without technical knowledge?
You need basic comfort with a VPS and command line. If that feels unfamiliar, there are managed hosting options that handle the server for you at a modest cost.

### What happens if Coolify development stops?
Because the source code is open, you can continue running whatever version you have indefinitely. You can also fork the project or switch to another tool at your own pace — no vendor can shut off your instance.

---
*Data sourced July 2026. Pricing and features change. Verify at [Netlify](https://netlify.com) and [Coolify](https://coolify.io) before making decisions.*
meta_description: Coolify is a free, self-hosted alternative to Netlify. Compare pricing, features, and migration steps. See full comparison.

# Salesforce vs EspoCRM (2026)

## Overview
Salesforce and EspoCRM are two popular customer relationship management (CRM) tools used by businesses to manage sales, marketing, and customer service. This comparison is beneficial for businesses looking to switch from a proprietary CRM to a self-hosted, open-source alternative, with the core use case being sales team management and the key reason to switch being cost savings or data ownership.

* Cost: Salesforce offers a range of pricing plans, while EspoCRM is free and self-hosted.
* Data Ownership: EspoCRM allows users to retain full ownership of their data, whereas Salesforce has stricter data ownership policies.
* Setup Complexity: Salesforce has a more complex setup process, while EspoCRM is relatively easier to set up.
* Scalability: Salesforce is highly scalable, but EspoCRM can also scale with proper server configuration.
* Feature Difference: Salesforce has a built-in AI-powered sales forecasting tool, while EspoCRM relies on third-party integrations for similar functionality.

| Aspect | Salesforce | EspoCRM |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $25-$300+/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | AGPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $1250-$15,000+/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $5,000-$60,000+/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Salesforce:**
* Highly scalable and reliable
* Wide range of integrations and features
* Strong customer support
* Customizable workflow automation
* Steep learning curve
**EspoCRM:**
* Free and self-hosted
* High degree of customizability
* Open-source community support
* Simple and intuitive interface

Salesforce is ideal for large enterprises with complex sales teams and a need for advanced features like AI-powered sales forecasting. 2. Prepare the data for import into EspoCRM by formatting it according to EspoCRM's import requirements.

4. Configure EspoCRM's workflow automation and customization features to match the previous Salesforce setup.

EspoCRM is a production-ready CRM solution for most users, offering a high degree of customizability and data ownership. However, one specific technical limitation worth knowing is that EspoCRM's built-in reporting features are limited, and users may need to rely on third-party integrations for advanced reporting. For businesses that prioritize data ownership and cost savings, EspoCRM is a clear choice, but for large enterprises with complex sales teams, Salesforce may still be the better option.

* Small businesses with fewer than 10 users who do not need advanced sales forecasting features
* Startups that prioritize data ownership and cost savings
* Teams with simple sales workflows that do not require complex customization
* Businesses that currently use other open-source tools and want to integrate with EspoCRM
* Companies with limited IT resources who want a simple, self-hosted CRM solution

## FAQ

While EspoCRM can scale with proper server configuration, it may not be the best choice for large enterprises with complex sales teams and a need for advanced features.

# Shopify vs WooCommerce (2026)

## Overview
Shopify and WooCommerce are two popular e-commerce platforms that enable businesses to create online stores and sell products. This comparison is beneficial for entrepreneurs, small business owners, and e-commerce teams who want to choose the best platform for their online store. The core use case for both tools is to provide a scalable and secure e-commerce solution, and the key reason someone would switch is to gain more control over their data and customization options.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Shopify offers a range of pricing plans, while WooCommerce is free to download and use, with costs limited to hosting and customization.
* Data ownership: Shopify stores data on its servers, while WooCommerce allows users to host their data on their own servers.
* Setup complexity: Shopify is generally easier to set up, with a more user-friendly interface, while WooCommerce requires more technical expertise.
* Scalability: Both platforms are scalable, but Shopify has more built-in features to support large stores, while WooCommerce relies on third-party plugins.
* Payment gateway integration: Shopify has a built-in payment gateway, while WooCommerce integrates with a range of third-party payment gateways, including PayPal and Stripe.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Shopify | WooCommerce |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $29-$299+/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | GPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | Approximately $29-$49/month (Basic Shopify plan) | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | Approximately $299-$499+/month (Advanced Shopify plan) | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
### Shopify
* Easy to set up and use
* Built-in payment gateway and shipping integrations
* Scalable and secure
* 24/7 customer support
* Limited customization options
### WooCommerce
* Highly customizable and extensible
* Free to download and use
* Self-hosted, giving users full control over their data
* Large community of developers and users
* Can be complex to set up and configure

## When to Choose Each
Shopify is a good choice for small to medium-sized businesses that want a easy-to-use, all-in-one e-commerce solution. It's ideal for teams with limited technical expertise who want to get started quickly. WooCommerce, on the other hand, is a good choice for larger businesses or those with more complex e-commerce needs. It's ideal for teams with technical expertise who want a high degree of customization and control over their online store.

## Migration Path
1. Export your Shopify store's data using the Shopify API or a third-party export tool.
2. Install WooCommerce on your self-hosted WordPress site.
3. Import your Shopify data into WooCommerce using a tool like the WooCommerce Importer or a third-party migration plugin.
4. Configure your WooCommerce store's settings and plugins to match your Shopify store's functionality.
5. Test your WooCommerce store to ensure that everything is working as expected.

## Our Take
WooCommerce is a production-ready e-commerce platform for most users, with a large community of developers and users who contribute to its development and support. However, one technical limitation worth knowing is that WooCommerce can be resource-intensive, requiring a robust hosting setup to support large stores. We recommend WooCommerce for businesses that want a high degree of customization and control over their online store, and Shopify for those who want a easy-to-use, all-in-one solution.

WooCommerce is a good choice for businesses that want to take advantage of the flexibility and customizability of WordPress. However, it may not be the best choice for businesses with limited technical expertise or those who want a simple, out-of-the-box solution. Shopify, on the other hand, is a good choice for businesses that want a easy-to-use, all-in-one e-commerce solution with built-in payment and shipping integrations.

In conclusion, the choice between Shopify and WooCommerce depends on your business's specific needs and requirements. If you want a high degree of customization and control over your online store, WooCommerce may be the better choice. However, if you want a easy-to-use, all-in-one solution with built-in payment and shipping integrations, Shopify may be the better choice.

## Who Should Switch
* Small businesses with limited technical expertise who want more control over their data and customization options
* Medium-sized businesses with complex e-commerce needs who want a more scalable and secure solution
* Large businesses with in-house development teams who want a high degree of customization and control over their online store
* E-commerce teams who want to take advantage of the flexibility and customizability of WordPress
* Businesses who want to save money on monthly subscription fees and have the technical expertise to self-host their online store

## FAQ
### Can I use WooCommerce with any WordPress theme?
Yes, WooCommerce can be used with any WordPress theme, but some themes are optimized for e-commerce and may provide a better user experience.

### Is Shopify more secure than WooCommerce?
Both Shopify and WooCommerce have robust security features, but Shopify's built-in security features may provide an additional layer of protection for businesses with limited technical expertise.

### Can I migrate my Shopify store to WooCommerce?
Yes, you can migrate your Shopify store to WooCommerce using a third-party migration plugin or by exporting your Shopify data and importing it into WooCommerce.

### Does WooCommerce have built-in payment gateway integrations?
No, WooCommerce does not have built-in payment gateway integrations, but it integrates with a range of third-party payment gateways, including PayPal and Stripe.

### Is WooCommerce free to use?
Yes, WooCommerce is free to download and use, but you may need to pay for hosting, customization, and third-party plugins.

# DocuSign vs DocuSeal (2026)

## Overview
DocuSign and DocuSeal are electronic signature tools that enable users to sign and send documents digitally. This comparison benefits individuals and organizations seeking to streamline their document signing processes, with a core use case of securely signing and managing documents. A key reason someone would switch from DocuSign to DocuSeal is to take advantage of DocuSeal's self-hosted option and potential cost savings.

## Key Differences
* Cost: DocuSign charges a per-user fee, while DocuSeal is free and self-hosted.
* Data ownership: DocuSeal allows users to maintain full control over their data, whereas DocuSign stores data on its servers.
* Setup complexity: DocuSeal requires more technical expertise to set up, especially for self-hosting, while DocuSign offers a more straightforward, cloud-based setup.
* Scalability: DocuSign is designed to handle large volumes of documents and users, while DocuSeal's scalability depends on the user's self-hosting infrastructure.
* Integration difference: DocuSign integrates with a wider range of third-party services, including popular CRM and productivity tools, while DocuSeal focuses on core electronic signature functionality.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | DocuSign | DocuSeal |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $15-$65+/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | AGPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $750-$3,250+/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $3,000-$13,000+/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**DocuSign:**
* Easy to use and set up
* Wide range of integrations with third-party services
* Robust security and compliance features
* Scalable and reliable infrastructure
* Good customer support
* Limited control over data storage and ownership
**DocuSeal:**
* Free and self-hosted, reducing costs
* Full control over data storage and ownership
* Customizable and flexible
* AGPL 3.0 license allows for community-driven development
* Limited integrations with third-party services
* Requires technical expertise for self-hosting
* Limited scalability without proper infrastructure

## When to Choose Each
DocuSign is suitable for large teams and enterprises that require a scalable, reliable, and easy-to-use electronic signature solution with a wide range of integrations. It is also a good choice for users who prioritize convenience and are willing to pay for a cloud-based service. On the other hand, DocuSeal is ideal for small to medium-sized teams, individuals, or organizations that value data ownership and control, and are comfortable with self-hosting and managing their own infrastructure.

## Migration Path
1. Export documents and templates from DocuSign in PDF format.
2. Set up a DocuSeal server and configure the necessary settings.
3. Use the DocuSeal import tool to transfer documents and templates from the exported PDF files.
4. Update any integrations or workflows to point to the new DocuSeal instance.
5. Test the migration to ensure all documents and functionality are working as expected.

## Our Take
DocuSeal is not yet production-ready for most users due to its limited scalability and lack of integrations with third-party services. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that DocuSeal requires a significant amount of technical expertise to set up and manage, especially for self-hosting. However, for users who value data ownership and control, and are comfortable with self-hosting, DocuSeal is a viable alternative to DocuSign, and we recommend considering it for small to medium-sized teams or individuals.

## Who Should Switch
* Small businesses with fewer than 10 employees who do not need advanced integrations
* Individuals who require a free, self-hosted electronic signature solution
* Teams with limited budgets who prioritize cost savings
* Organizations that value data ownership and control
* Developers who want to customize and extend their electronic signature solution

## FAQ
### Can I use DocuSeal for free?
Yes, DocuSeal is free and self-hosted, reducing costs for users. However, users will need to cover server costs.
### Is DocuSeal as secure as DocuSign?
DocuSeal has robust security features, but its security depends on the user's self-hosting infrastructure and configuration.
### Can I integrate DocuSeal with my existing CRM?
Currently, DocuSeal has limited integrations with third-party services, including CRMs. However, its API allows for custom integrations.
### How do I migrate from DocuSign to DocuSeal?
The migration process involves exporting documents and templates from DocuSign, setting up a DocuSeal server, and using the import tool to transfer data.
### Is DocuSeal suitable for large enterprises?
No, DocuSeal is not yet suitable for large enterprises due to its limited scalability and lack of advanced integrations.

# Sentry vs GlitchTip (2026)

## Overview
Sentry and GlitchTip are error tracking and monitoring tools used by software development teams to identify and resolve issues in their applications. This comparison is beneficial for teams currently using Sentry who are considering switching to GlitchTip, possibly due to cost or data ownership concerns. The core use case for both tools is to provide insights into application errors, and the key reason someone would switch is to gain more control over their data or reduce costs.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Sentry offers a free plan with limited features, while GlitchTip is free and open-source, allowing for self-hosting.
* Data ownership: GlitchTip allows for complete data ownership since it can be self-hosted, whereas Sentry stores data on its servers.
* Setup complexity: Sentry has a more straightforward setup process, while GlitchTip requires more technical expertise for self-hosting.
* Scalability: Sentry is designed to handle large volumes of data and traffic, while GlitchTip's scalability depends on the self-hosting environment.
* Integration difference: Sentry has native integration with more third-party tools and services, while GlitchTip's integrations are more limited but can be extended through its open-source nature.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Sentry | GlitchTip |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | Free / $26-$80+/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | BSD |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | Approximately $26-$52/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | Approximately $104-$208/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
### Sentry
* Pros:
  + Easy setup and integration with many services
  + Scalable and reliable infrastructure
  + Offers a free plan with limited features
  + Strong support and community
  + Native integration with many third-party tools
* Cons:
  + Can be expensive for large teams or high-volume projects
  + Data is stored on Sentry's servers, which may be a concern for some teams
  + Limited customization options for the free plan
  + Proprietary license

### GlitchTip
* Pros:
  + Completely free and open-source
  + Allows for self-hosting and complete data ownership
  + Customizable and extensible through its open-source nature
  + Can be more cost-effective for large teams or high-volume projects
  + BSD license
* Cons:
  + Requires more technical expertise for self-hosting
  + Limited native integrations with third-party tools
  + May require additional setup and configuration for scalability
  + Limited support and community compared to Sentry
  + Dependence on self-hosting environment for reliability and uptime

## When to Choose Each
Sentry is a good choice for teams that prioritize ease of use, scalability, and strong support. It's suitable for small to medium-sized teams that don't have the technical expertise or resources for self-hosting and are willing to pay for the convenience. On the other hand, GlitchTip is ideal for teams that value data ownership, customization, and cost-effectiveness. It's suitable for larger teams or projects that require complete control over their data and are willing to invest time and resources into self-hosting and customization.

## Migration Path
1. Export your data from Sentry in JSON format using the Sentry API or the export tool.
2. Set up a GlitchTip instance on your server, either manually or using a containerization platform like Docker.
3. Use the GlitchTip import tool to import your exported data from Sentry.
4. Configure any additional settings, such as project settings, user permissions, and integrations, to match your Sentry setup.
5. Test your GlitchTip instance to ensure that all features and integrations are working as expected.

## Our Take
GlitchTip is not yet production-ready for most users due to its limited support and community, as well as its requirement for technical expertise for self-hosting. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that GlitchTip's scalability depends on the self-hosting environment, which can be a concern for large teams or high-volume projects. However, for teams that value data ownership and customization, and are willing to invest time and resources into self-hosting and customization, GlitchTip is a viable alternative to Sentry.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams (less than 10 users) that don't need native integration with many third-party tools
* Teams that prioritize data ownership and customization
* Large teams (more than 50 users) that require cost-effectiveness and are willing to invest in self-hosting
* Projects that require complete control over their data and are willing to invest time and resources into self-hosting and customization
* Teams that don't need strong support and community, and are willing to rely on their own technical expertise

Yes, GlitchTip is completely free and open-source, allowing for self-hosting and complete data ownership.
